books.section: Topic 8.13 The environment and natural resources from 1968 to 1980

primary_sources: Aerial photograph of the Santa Barbara oil spill, 1969 (U.S. Geological Survey)

source: original; stimulus photograph viewed before writing

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: aerial view of oil rising near Union Oil Platform A, Santa Barbara Channel, 1969, public domain (U.S. Geological Survey photograph, via Wikimedia Commons). Spill facts verified against Clarke and Hemphill, 'The Santa Barbara Oil Spill: A Retrospective' (2002) and the Sierra Club account: blowout January 28, 1969; about three million gallons over eleven days; 35 miles of coastline. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.13).
stimulus.text:
The photograph is an aerial view taken during the Santa Barbara oil spill of 1969. It shows an offshore drilling rig standing in dark water, with a pale patch of oil rising to the surface at the upper left and a disturbed ring of water around the rig.

On January 28, 1969, a well on Union Oil's Platform A, about six miles off Santa Barbara, California, blew out. Roughly three to four million gallons of crude oil escaped over about eleven days, coating about 35 miles of coastline and killing thousands of seabirds. The spill was the largest in American history at the time.

options.text: A fishing fleet hauling in a catch off Santa Barbara.
options.misconception: The image shows a single drilling rig, not fishing boats with nets.

options.text: A naval battle between American and foreign ships.
options.misconception: The image shows no warships or fighting, only a drilling rig in oily water.

options.text: A beach crowded with tourists on a summer day.
options.misconception: The image is an aerial view of open water, not a beach with people.

options.text: Oil rising to the surface near an offshore drilling rig.

rationales.A: The image shows a single drilling rig, not fishing boats with nets.
rationales.B: The image shows no warships or fighting, only a drilling rig in oily water.
rationales.C: The image is an aerial view of open water, not a beach with people.
rationales.D: The photograph shows a drilling rig in dark water, with oil rising to the surface beside it.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph is an aerial view of open water, with a drilling rig at the right.
2. The pale patch at the upper left and the disturbed ring around the rig are oil rising to the surface.
3. Background: The text dates the scene to the January 1969 blowout on Union Oil's Platform A.
Remember: Start with what the image literally shows, then use the text to name the event.
